questions.question:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

If I was a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains a grammatical error in the conditional clause "If I was a king."
 
• When expressing hypothetical or unreal situations, the verb "was" should be replaced with "were" in the clause following "if."
 
• The correct phrasing is "If I were a king," which aligns with the subjunctive mood used for hypothetical conditions.
 
• This correction ensures the sentence is grammatically accurate and conveys the intended meaning properly.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"If I were a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "on my country"** – This is incorrect as the correct preposition to use is "from" in this context.
 
• **Option 2: "my best by remove poverty"** – This is grammatically incorrect as "by remove" should be replaced with "by removing."
 
• **Option 4: "I would has tried"** – This is grammatically incorrect as "has" should be replaced with "have" in this context.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The manager decided to __disclose a secret__ and address the issue at the team meeting.

options.text: hit the nail on the head

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "spill the beans".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"spill the beans"** means to disclose a secret or reveal confidential information, often unintentionally. (राज़ खोल देना)

 
 
• **Example:** She accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party during lunch.
 
 
 
• **"Bury the hatchet"** means to reconcile or make peace with someone after a conflict or disagreement. (मित्रता करना)
 
 
• **Example:** After years of rivalry, the two leaders decided to bury the hatchet and work together.
 
 
 
• **"Hit the nail on the head"** means to describe or do something exactly right or perfectly. (सटीक बात कहना)
 
 
• **Example:** When she suggested the new strategy, she really hit the nail on the head.
 
 
 
• **"Sweep it under the rug"** refers to hiding a problem or issue instead of addressing it. (समस्या को नजरअंदाज करना)
 
 
• **Example:** Instead of discussing their mistake, they tried to sweep it under the rug.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "spill the beans".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Bury the hatchet** (मित्रता करना): To reconcile or make peace after a conflict or disagreement.

 
 
• **Example:** The two teams buried the hatchet after the heated match.
 
 
 
• **Hit the nail on the head** (सटीक बात कहना): To describe something accurately or do something perfectly.
 
 
• **Example:** Her explanation of the problem really hit the nail on the head.
 
 
 
• **Sweep it under the rug** (समस्या को नजरअंदाज करना): To hide or avoid dealing with a problem or issue.
 
 
• **Example:** They decided to sweep the financial issues under the rug instead of fixing them.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The blanket gifted by my granny is __softer__ and cozy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"soft"** means smooth, gentle, or pleasant to touch; it often refers to texture or a quality that lacks hardness or firmness. (नरम, कोमल)

 
 
• **Example:** The pillow felt soft against her cheek.
 
 
 
• The word **"cozy"** means comfortable, warm, and pleasant, especially in an environment or setting. (आरामदायक)
 
 
• **Example:** She wrapped herself in a cozy blanket and sipped tea.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "soft" is the correct choice to simplify and accurately convey the meaning of the blanket's texture without unnecessary comparison or modifiers.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1: "more soft"** (अधिक नरम): This phrase is grammatically incorrect as "soft" is already a simple adjective and does not require "more" for comparison. The correct comparative form is "softer."

 
 
• **Example:** Incorrect: This blanket is more soft than that one.
 
• **Correct:** This blanket is softer than that one.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "softly"** (धीरे से): "Softly" is an adverb and does not fit the context of describing the texture of the blanket.
 
 
• **Example:** She spoke softly to calm the baby.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "softest"** (सबसे नरम): "Softest" is the superlative form of "soft," used when comparing three or more items. It is incorrect in this context because no comparison is implied.
 
 
• **Example:** This is the softest blanket I’ve ever owned.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They was / celebrating their / Silver wedding anniversary / next month in Dubai.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. They was .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence contains a grammatical error in the first segment, **"They was"**.
 
• The subject **"They"** is plural, and therefore, the correct verb form is **"were"**, not **"was"**.
 
• Correct grammar usage would be: **"They were"**.
 
• The other segments of the sentence are grammatically correct.

Correct sentence: *They were celebrating their Silver wedding anniversary next month in Dubai.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The use of **"next month"** indicates a future event, but in this case, the verb tense remains in the past progressive (*were celebrating*) to describe an intention or plan in informal usage.
 
• **Subject-verb agreement:** Always match the verb form to the subject in terms of number (singular or plural).

questions.question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

Almost as wide as he was tall, he had a __voracious__ appetite for food and drink and a rollicking personality to match.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3 (Insatiable)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Voracious"** means having a strong, insatiable appetite for something, particularly food or drink, or an eager desire for an activity. (अत्यधिक भूखा या लालची)

 
 
• **Example:** He was a voracious reader, devouring books one after another.
 
 
 
• **"Insatiable"** refers to something that cannot be satisfied or fulfilled, often used in the context of hunger or desire. (अतृप्त या जिसकी पूर्ति न हो सके)
 
 
• **Example:** Her insatiable curiosity led her to explore different cultures and languages.
 
 
 
• Both "voracious" and "insatiable" share the connotation of an intense and unquenchable appetite or desire.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3 (Insatiable)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Vehement** (प्रबल): Showing strong and passionate intensity in emotions or actions.

 
 
• **Example:** She made a vehement argument against the new policy.
 
 
 
• **Imminent** (आसन्न): About to happen or occur very soon.
 
 
• **Example:** The dark clouds signaled that a storm was imminent.
 
 
 
• **Venerable** (आदरणीय): Commanding respect because of age, wisdom, or character.
 
 
• **Example:** The venerable professor was honored for his years of service to the university.

Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The unexpected guest at the party was __a bull in a China shop.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (careless and damaging)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"a bull in a China shop"** is an idiom used to describe someone who behaves clumsily and causes damage, either physically or metaphorically. (असावधान और हानिकारक)

 
 
• **Example:** John's loud and disruptive behavior in the library was like a bull in a China shop.
 
 
 
• **Careless and damaging** refers to behavior that lacks caution and results in harm or destruction. (लापरवाह और हानिकारक)
 
 
• **Example:** The careless handling of delicate equipment led to damaging consequences.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "a bull in a China shop" can be aptly substituted with "careless and damaging."

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (careless and damaging)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Influential and meticulous** (प्रभावशाली और सूक्ष्म): Refers to someone who has a strong impact and pays great attention to detail.

 
 
• **Example:** Her influential and meticulous leadership transformed the company's fortunes.
 
 
 
• **Careful and compassionate** (सावधान और दयालु): Refers to someone who acts with caution and kindness.
 
 
• **Example:** The doctor was careful and compassionate while treating the injured child.
 
 
 
• **Leisurely and relaxed** (आरामदायक और शांत): Refers to someone who is unhurried and at ease.
 
 
• **Example:** We spent a leisurely and relaxed afternoon by the lake.

• Understanding context is crucial to choosing the correct phrasal verb.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'illuminate' from the given sentence.

The toughest and most typical question in the examination was to elucidate a particular theory related to friction in physics.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Elucidate**.

• **Example:** The teacher used examples to illuminate the concept of gravity for the students.
 
 
 
• **"Elucidate"** is a synonym of "Illuminate," and it means to explain something clearly or make it easier to understand. (व्याख्या करना या स्पष्ट करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The professor took extra time to elucidate the complex theory to the class.
 
 
 
• Thus, "Elucidate" closely relates to "Illuminate" in meaning, as both refer to making something clear or understandable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. **Elucidate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

• **Example:** It's typical of him to arrive late to meetings.
 
 
 
• **Particular** (विशिष्ट): Refers to a specific or distinct thing.
 
 
• **Example:** She has a particular interest in ancient history.
 
 
 
• **Theory** (सिद्धांत): A system of ideas intended to explain something.
 
 
• **Example:** Einstein's theory of relativity revolutionized physics.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

Everyone in the room was in a __jolly __and relaxed mood.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. No substitution required .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically correct as it stands.
 
• The phrase "in a jolly and relaxed mood" is appropriate and does not require substitution.
 
• Other options such as "most jolly," "jollier," and "more jollier" are either incorrect or do not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• "Most jolly" suggests a superlative degree, which is unnecessary in this context. "Jollier" and "more jollier" are either incorrect or redundant.

Correct sentence: *Everyone in the room was in a jolly and relaxed mood*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative and Superlative Usage:**

 
 
• **Comparative (e.g., jollier):** Used when comparing two things or people.
 
• **Superlative (e.g., most jolly):** Used when comparing more than two things or people.
 
• In this sentence, no comparison is being made, so there is no need for a comparative or superlative form.
 
 
 
• **Redundancy:** "More jollier" is incorrect because it combines both "more" and the comparative form "jollier," which is redundant.

questions.question:
Select the word segment from the given options that substitutes the highlighted word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully: -

Each of the participants__ were __given a certificate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. was given.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"Each of the participants."** The word **"each"** is singular and requires a singular verb.
 
• In the given sentence, the verb **"were"** is incorrect because it is plural, which does not agree with the singular subject **"each."**
 
• The correct singular verb to use is **"was."**

Correct sentence: *Each of the participants **was given** a certificate.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:**

 
 
• When **"each"** is used as the subject, it is always singular and requires a singular verb (e.g., was, has, is).
 
• Example: Each of the students **is** responsible for their own work.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Using a plural verb with **"each."**
 
• Incorrect: Each of the members **are** present.
 
• Correct: Each of the members **is** present.
